topSignals.title: First appearance in this digest: Rystad Energy discloses a ~9 GW fuel-cell "order book" for AI data centers and two concrete deployment-speed case studies — Bloom delivered power to Oracle's Utah site in under two months; Nebius's New Jersey site cleared planning-board approval within three months of signing.
topSignals.text: A Reuters-sourced piece (published Oct 23, surfaced only in today's research pass) adds granular detail that has not previously appeared alongside this digest's standing Rystad $30B/2030 market-size figure (logged since June): roughly 9 GW of cumulative fuel-cell orders now sit behind framework agreements with Oracle, AEP, Equinix and Brookfield — Rystad cautions these framework deals may not be firm orders for their full stated capacity — and annual manufacturing capacity is tracked toward 4 GW/yr by 2030 from ~1.8 GW/yr today (consistent with the already-logged figure). Bloom's commercial chief is quoted saying that for 100+ MW projects, site readiness, permitting and grid/gas infrastructure — not the fuel-cell technology itself — now set the critical path. So what for INOCEL: the Oracle-Utah (<2 months) and Nebius-NJ (3-month planning approval) cases are usable, company-disclosed timeline anchors for the LCOE model's deployment-speed/schedule-risk assumptions, and the explicit framework-vs-firm-order caveat on the 9 GW figure is a useful caution against overstating near-term contracted volume when benchmarking order momentum against INOCEL's own pipeline. BNN Bloomberg/Reuters

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new item since the Sept 21 Metrosert testing-cooperation announcement, confirmed by direct newsroom fetch today — 38 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed by direct fetch today — 63 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by SAF/ammonia/e-methanol news, out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Bloom Energy, Ceres Power) — completes this cycle's full 8-company roster (started Oct 25 with FuelCell Energy/Mitsubishi Power; continued Oct 27 Sunfire/SolydEra, Oct 28 Kyocera/Aisin): no new stack/cell-technology items for either. Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 5, round 2 (Watt Fuel Cell, OxEon Energy, Nexceris, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol), 7-day lookback: no new items for any of the six; results repeated the standing Miura/Ceres 4.2kW SOFC-CHP Japan launch, Nexceris's $60M SOEC scale-up deal, and MHI's SOEC test-module history, all already logged or pre-2026-vintage.

Tier 3 sweep — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR SK ecoplant": no new item; results repeated the standing Reverion $175M Series B, the 2023-vintage Bloom/SK ecoplant 500 MW sales agreement, and Doosan-Reverion's Sept 18 $78M stack order.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, hearing Dec 7), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ — first power block reported ready Oct 22; block capacity undisclosed; site not yet operational), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

lcoe.text: Carry-forward, unchanged:* Virginia data-center electricity tax ($0.011/kWh); PJM Reliability Backstop ceiling (~$202.6/kW-year avoided-cost benchmark, filing suspended pending Feb 28, 2027 paper hearing); PJM's proposed 50 MW behind-the-meter netting threshold (pending FERC approval, 3-year grandfather); FCEL Torrington capex ($200-275M for 350-500 MW/yr by 2028); AEP/Bloom bundled utility-purchase benchmark ($2,944/kW capital+service); Germany's Netzpaket redispatch-curtailment risk (18-20% uncompensated annual-output exposure) for non-islanded SOFC deployments.
